about: Space Hunter's cleanup items for Linux. Each item is one row in the app. See CONTRIBUTING.md for every field. Items with "admin": true clean system folders after one password prompt; their folders must also be on the built-in list in linux/src/engine.rs.

items.name: Old temporary files
items.what: Scratch files that apps, installers and AI agents such as Claude Code or Codex leave in /tmp and /var/tmp.
items.deletes: Your own files there that haven't changed for a day. Other users' and the system's files are never touched.
items.safe: Yes. Files changed within the last day are left alone, so running apps keep theirs.
items.after: Apps recreate what they need. Many systems also clear /tmp on restart.

items.name: Thumbnail cache
items.what: Small preview pictures your file manager makes for photos, videos and documents.
items.deletes: Every thumbnail in ~/.cache/thumbnails.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: Folders with many pictures show previews a little slower the first time.

items.name: Browser caches
items.short: Sites load slower once; logins kept
items.what: Copies of web pages, images and scripts kept by Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Vivaldi, Edge, Opera and Firefox.
items.deletes: The cache folders only. On Linux these live apart from your browser profile.
items.safe: Yes. Passwords, cookies, history, bookmarks and extensions are NOT touched.
items.after: Sites load a little slower once. Quit the browsers first for a full clean.

items.name: Chat app caches
items.short: Apps open slower once; messages kept
items.what: Discord, Slack and Teams keep a web cache, like a browser.
items.deletes: Their Cache, Code Cache and GPUCache folders.
items.safe: Yes. Messages, sign-ins and settings are untouched.
items.after: Quit the apps first for a full clean.

items.name: AI app caches & logs (e.g. Claude)
items.short: Apps open slower once; chats kept
items.what: AI desktop apps such as Claude keep a web cache, a GPU cache and logs, like a browser does.
items.deletes: Those folders only. Not your chats, agent sessions or settings.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: Quit the app first for a full clean.

items.name: Code editor caches & logs
items.what: VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and JetBrains IDEs keep caches, compiled code and logs.
items.deletes: Cache, CachedData, Code Cache, GPUCache and logs; JetBrains' cache folder.
items.safe: Yes. Extensions, settings and projects are untouched.
items.after: Rebuilt on the next start. A JetBrains IDE re-indexes your project once, which takes a few minutes.

items.name: npm, Yarn, pip and uv download caches
items.what: Download caches for JavaScript and Python packages that you or an AI agent installed.
items.deletes: Those cache folders. Same as 'npm cache clean --force', 'pip cache purge' and similar.
items.safe: Yes. Projects' node_modules and virtual environments are untouched.
items.after: The next install downloads again and needs internet.

items.name: Go build cache
items.short: The next build compiles from scratch
items.what: Compiled pieces Go keeps to make builds faster.
items.deletes: ~/.cache/go-build. Same as 'go clean -cache'.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build of each project takes longer.

items.name: Downloaded system updates (apt)
items.what: Ubuntu, Debian and Mint keep a copy of every update package after installing it.
items.deletes: The .deb files in /var/cache/apt/archives. Same as 'sudo apt clean'.
items.safe: Yes. The updates stay installed.
items.after: Nothing changes. Linux asks for your password once to clean system folders.

items.name: Downloaded system updates (dnf, zypper)
items.what: Fedora and openSUSE keep downloaded packages and package lists.
items.deletes: Everything in those cache folders. Same as 'sudo dnf clean all'.
items.safe: Yes. The updates stay installed.
items.after: The next update downloads the package lists again.

items.name: Crash dumps
items.short: Old crash reports; needs your password
items.what: Snapshots of apps that crashed, kept so developers can look at them.
items.deletes: Every crash dump in those folders.
items.safe: Yes; you lose the old reports, which matter only to someone fixing that crash.
items.after: Nothing changes.

items.name: Trash
items.what: Files you moved to the Trash from your file manager.
items.deletes: Everything in your Trash.
items.safe: Only if you're sure; this is permanent.
items.after: Nothing can be restored.

items.name: System logs older than 2 weeks
items.short: Older logs go; needs your password
items.what: The system journal: messages from Linux and its services, kept for troubleshooting.
items.deletes: Log entries older than 2 weeks. Same as 'sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=14d'.
items.safe: Yes, unless you're investigating a problem from more than 2 weeks ago.
items.after: Recent logs stay.

items.name: Old package versions (pacman)
items.short: No rolling back; needs your password
items.what: Arch and Manjaro keep every version of every package they've installed.
items.deletes: Everything in /var/cache/pacman/pkg. Same as 'sudo pacman -Scc'.
items.safe: Yes, but you can no longer go back to an older version of a package without downloading it.
items.after: Downgrading a package needs internet.

items.name: Downloaded AI models
items.what: AI models and datasets downloaded by Python tools (Hugging Face, PyTorch) and Ollama. Some are many GB each.
items.deletes: Everything in those model folders.
items.safe: Only if you don't need them offline.
items.after: Scripts and Ollama download them again.

items.name: AI tool runtimes (e.g. Codex)
items.what: Runtimes and browsers that command-line AI tools such as Codex and Playwright download for themselves.
items.deletes: Those folders.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The tool's next run is slower.

items.name: Rust (Cargo) downloads
items.what: Cargo keeps every crate it downloaded, both packed and unpacked.
items.deletes: The registry cache, unpacked sources and git checkouts. Installed tools in ~/.cargo/bin are kept.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build downloads crates again and needs internet.

items.name: Gradle and Maven downloads
items.what: Java and Android build tools keep every library they downloaded.
items.deletes: Gradle's caches and Maven's repository.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build downloads libraries again and needs internet.

items.name: Old AI agent chat history (Claude Code, Codex)
items.short: Those chats can't be resumed; memory kept
items.what: AI coding agents such as Claude Code (~/.claude) and Codex (~/.codex) save every conversation, sub-tasks and big tool outputs, plus checkpoints for undo.
items.deletes: Conversation and checkpoint files not changed within the age you set. Agents' memory folders (such as Claude's memory) are always skipped.
items.safe: Only for conversations you'll never reopen. Recent ones are protected by the age rule.
items.after: Those conversations can't be resumed or rewound.

items.name: Old installers & archives in Downloads
items.short: Installers and archives only, top level
items.what: Packages, AppImages, disk images and archives that pile up in Downloads after you've installed or unpacked them.
items.deletes: Only .deb, .rpm, .AppImage, .iso, .zip, .tar.gz and similar files sitting directly in Downloads, untouched for the age you set (30 days by default). Sub-folders and every other file type are never touched.
items.safe: Usually. Check the folder first if you keep installers you can't download again.
items.after: You'd need to download those installers again.
